elements.desc: Cream outro: logo slot (default abstract SVG mark), slogan and url springing in, with a short input fade.
elements.use: End of a clip/overlay piece, sign-off.

elements.title: Outro Title Stack
elements.desc: Two-line outro (heavy title scale spring, italic subtitle rising) plus a small credit footer fading in.
elements.use: beat-synced / lyric reels needing this piece.

elements.title: Overhead Camera Moves
elements.desc: Overhead-angle storytelling in two variants. tilt = a page hinged at its lower edge rises from a glowing flat band to upright (overshoot, then settle); tabletop = flat page cards pan past on a grid desk, one is picked and the camera dives onto it. Use for openings and page-to-page transitions where the pitch angle itself tells the story.
elements.use: single-page establishing opening (tilt) or "scan several pages, pick one" transition/opening (tabletop).

elements.title: Overlay Scene Card
elements.desc: Transparent overlay: floating card (eyebrow + accent-word headline, spring rise) with pop tags, scheduled by beat ranges at 120 BPM, fading in the last 8 src frames; clip is a children slot. Exports OverlaySceneCards and SceneCard.
elements.use: Captions/explainer cards over a supplied clip.

elements.title: Page Turn Transitions
elements.desc: Barn-door split - the old page shows a hairline, cracks open into a light seam, both halves accelerate out sideways, and the new page rises from under it with an over-exposed beam. Treats pages as physical slabs.
elements.use: chapter-level page changes where the new replaces the old (version 3 to version 4).

elements.title: Page Waterfall Wall
elements.desc: Three columns of page cards scroll endlessly on a tilted wall (perspective plus rotateX 20); loop times differ and the middle column runs the other way so the columns read as independent; the camera pushes in slowly on the outer layer.
elements.use: "too much content to show" flowing overviews, ambient backgrounds, continuing a wall entrance.

elements.title: Panel Grid Moves
elements.desc: Comic-panel rhythm: one lens shot from three camera positions is cut into stacked panels on the beat (hard cuts with a paper-cut seam), then the last panel's edge sweeps up and becomes a poster. Use for one subject shown from several angles.
elements.use: a single product or subject in several views, comic or storyboard-style sections, a beat-led reveal where the panel change is the drum hit.

elements.title: Paper Card World
elements.desc: Light off-white world with floating white rounded cards: four layered soft shadows, spring rise then gentle drift; dark only inside one card. Scene/layout shell for UI-style explainers.
elements.use: clean product/explainer scenes, dashboards, anything that should feel calm and premium.

elements.title: Paper Cutout Parallax
elements.desc: Layered paper cut-outs with white edges and hard shadows, stop-motion stepped at 12fps with a 24fps parallax camera and split-pin rotating joints
elements.use: music/fashion/kids/editorial scene backgrounds or hero scenes

elements.title: Paper Title Card
elements.desc: A one-line value proposition stamps onto a paper ground word by word (scale 1.28 to 1 with blur to 0), one italic accent word is set in the accent colour, a short accent underline closes it, and a mono sub-line rolls a number digit by digit.
elements.use: a chapter or transition card with a value claim; a breathing card between two high-energy shots; a feature lead-in before a product shot; a title that should match a paper or ink-toned product look.

elements.title: Particle Galaxy 3D
elements.desc: About 6000 additive point sprites in a three-arm spiral galaxy that reform (staggered, with a glow burst) into a ringed planet formation; camera drifts. Word-free.
elements.use: intro/transition backgrounds, hype beds, cosmic or tech themes, reform-to-ring reveal.

elements.title: Particle Glyph Assembly
elements.desc: Seeded particles spiral in from outside the frame and settle on the lit cells of a block-font word, then breathe. Targets come from a font grid, no canvas readback. Use for titles and slogans.
elements.use: hero titles, slogans, product names.

elements.title: Particles Orb 3D
elements.desc: About 1100 points on a rotating sphere that scatter into a ring and gather back on a 3 s loop; level-reactive size.
elements.use: AI/voice reels, loading and "thinking" beats, logo-less hero.

elements.title: Path Text
elements.desc: Text riding an SVG path, textPath startOffset sliding along it, optional outline
elements.use: curved/ribbon headline, wavy tickers

elements.title: Pen Follow Line
elements.desc: One ink polyline draws at constant 800px/s, camera pans to keep the pen tip mid-frame, closed loop floods with colour.
elements.use: minimal/luxury ads, whiteboard explainers, one-stroke logos

elements.title: Pixel FX: Achievement
elements.desc: A toast slides in on speed lines and settles; a gold medal pops onto it in a burst of sparkles, a shine sweeps the whole toast, then it slides away.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, ui moments (ui, achievement, toast, medal).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Arcane orb
elements.desc: A floating orb of smoky violet glass with a swirl turning round a white-hot heart, two tilted rings of light orbiting behind and in front.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, arcane moments (arcane, orb, sphere, magic).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Aurora
elements.desc: Rippling curtains of green-to-violet light over a starfield: folding hems burn bright, rays shimmer up into violet, and the whole sky slowly breathes.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, weather moments (weather, aurora, northern lights, sky).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Ball lightning
elements.desc: A crackling ball of plasma drifts on a wandering loop, spitting arcs off its skin and leaving a wake of fading motes, and zaps the floor when it dips low.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, lightning moments (lightning, electric, plasma, orb).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Barrel explosion
elements.desc: An explosive barrel shudders, its lid bulging and spitting flame, then blows: a fireball column, staves and the lid flying, burning fuel splashed over the floor.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, explosions moments (explosion, barrel, fire, smoke).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Bat
elements.desc: A bat flaps in four snappy wing frames along a figure-eight, its body lifting on each downbeat, moonlight on its wing bones, red eyes glowing and glinting.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, critters moments (critter, bat, night, flying).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Big explosion
elements.desc: A huge ground blast in three beats: a white dome, a rolling fireball that climbs into a mushrooming smoke column, heavy rocks, and fires left burning.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, explosions moments (explosion, fire, smoke, debris).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Black hole
elements.desc: A tilted disk of banded rings turns round a black hole, its far side bent up over the top and under the bottom; debris spirals in, stretches and is swallowed.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, shadow moments (shadow, black-hole, void, space).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Blizzard
elements.desc: Snow driven almost flat by a gale: streaks at three depths race past, gusts throw translucent sheets of snow across the sky and spindrift streams off the drifts.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, weather moments (weather, blizzard, snow, wind).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Brazier
elements.desc: An iron bowl on a tripod heaped with glowing coals and a big roaring fire, sparks and embers streaming up off it, light on the iron and the floor.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, fire moments (fire, brazier, prop, light).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Bubbles
elements.desc: Bubbles stream up from a vent of pebbles, wobbling and swelling as they rise, flare as they cross shafts of light from the surface, then dome up and pop there.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, water moments (water, bubbles, underwater, vent).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Butterfly
elements.desc: An iridescent butterfly wanders a loop in bursts of quick wingbeats and open-winged glides, its veined, spotted wings shedding a twinkling trail of glowing dust.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, critters moments (critter, butterfly, insect, flying).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Campfire
elements.desc: Crossed logs on a bed of coals and a lively fire: tongues that lick and leap, popping sparks, embers drifting up, smoke curling off, a warm pool of light.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, fire moments (fire, campfire, prop, light).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Candle
elements.desc: A wax candle in a brass dish: a calm flame with a blue root that sways and stretches, a halo of light, motes drifting in it, a bead of wax running down a drip.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, fire moments (fire, candle, prop, light).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Cartoon POW
elements.desc: A comic-book hit: a jagged two-tone burst star slams in with a shake and boiling edges, POW! drops in letter by letter, action lines fly, then it all snaps away.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, explosions moments (cartoon, comic, pow, hit).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Cherry blossoms
elements.desc: Pink petals flutter down on a spring breeze, tumbling in little spirals and flashing as they catch the light, with a few whole blossoms spinning among them.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, weather moments (weather, cherry blossom, sakura, petals).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Chest open
elements.desc: A banded chest rattles with gold light leaking from its seam, the lid kicks open, rays fan up, and coins and gems arc out, bounce, glint and get collected.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, pickups moments (pickup, chest, treasure, loot).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Coin collect
elements.desc: A coin bursts into a fountain of spinning coins that hang, then zip one by one into a HUD counter that pops and ticks up, glints and folds away.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, ui moments (ui, coins, pickup, reward).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Coin drop
elements.desc: An enemy goes up in a soft poof and gold coins spin out of it, bounce with a glint on each hit, settle on the floor, twinkle, and wink out one by one.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, spawn moments (spawn, death, loot, coins).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Coin spin
elements.desc: A thick gold coin turning on its edge: an embossed star face, a reeded rim showing as it goes edge-on, a flash sweeping the face, bobbing over its shadow.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, pickups moments (pickup, coin, gold, money).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Combo counter
elements.desc: x5 COMBO rockets in on streaming speed lines, smearing, and slams to a stop: a white flash, a ring, sparks; it pulses while a timer bar drains, then whooshes out.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, ui moments (ui, combo, counter, combat).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Confetti
elements.desc: Two party poppers bang one after the other: paper bits and curly streamers burst out, stall, then tumble and flutter down, flipping, and settle on the floor.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, ui moments (ui, celebration, confetti, party).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Countdown
elements.desc: 3, 2, 1 slam into a timer ring that drains like a burning fuse, throwing sparks; then GO! bursts out as the ring blows into a shockwave with rays.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, ui moments (ui, countdown, start, timer).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Critical hit
elements.desc: A critical hit: a jagged starburst slams in white and overshoots, a ring breaks into flying arcs, sparks streak off, shards tumble to the floor under a big flare.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, impacts moments (impact, hit, crit, critical).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Crit number
elements.desc: CRIT 128! slams in huge and white over a jagged starburst with a hard shake and speed lines, cools to fire, holds with a shine, then pops into sparks.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, ui moments (ui, critical, damage, number).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Damage number
elements.desc: A red -27 punches out of a hit spark, white for a frame, arcs up, lands with a squash and a little hop, then fades as it lifts away.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, ui moments (ui, damage, number, combat).

elements.title: Pixel FX: Eclipse
elements.desc: A black moon over the sun: a breathing pearl corona with long streamers, a thin white rim, and one diamond bead blazing on its edge.
elements.use: pixel-art/retro/game-style reels, shadow moments (shadow, eclipse, moon, sun).

elements.use: retro/game/lofi backgrounds, music or tech intros.

elements.title: Pixel Dissolve Transition
elements.desc: Scene A breaks into square pixels: cells of B grow open in a seeded order (random blended with a diagonal sweep) with a glint on each cell. Use for digital, game or glitch-adjacent cuts.
elements.use: tech, gaming, retro, data scenes.

elements.title: Pixel Tile Materialize
elements.desc: An illustration sliced into tiles flies in from seeded scatter poses, then a red box hops and deletes cells by fragment burst or binary fill. Use for redaction, data-wipe and tech reveals.
elements.use: redaction, data deletion, glitchy reveals.

elements.title: Pixel Upscale
elements.desc: Draw a scene on a native 180x320 pixel grid (the 9:16 version of 320x180) with a 16-colour palette, then upscale x6 with no smoothing; includes sprites, dither, pixel font
elements.use: game trailers, nostalgia, year-in-review.

elements.title: Planet Ring 3D
elements.desc: Banded gas planet with a tilted ring and an orbiting moon over a star-dust background; slow spin and camera drift.
elements.use: space/science/astronomy reels, title backdrops.

elements.title: Plasma Orb
elements.desc: Round orb filled with drifting, blurred colour blobs (mesh-gradient look) clipped to a disc; blobs swirl faster and swell with the audio level.
elements.use: AI-assistant/voice/music reels: listening, speaking and thinking beats.

elements.title: Polaroid Strip
elements.desc: White-bordered stills rising with alternating tilt and stagger, as a thumbnail row or a fanned stack.
elements.use: Showing frames/moments, contact-sheet feel, freeze-frame payoffs.

elements.title: Pop Captions
elements.desc: Vertical-social captions (1-4 words) that pop on the spoken beat with a scale overshoot and one accent-colour word
elements.use: Reels/Shorts/TikTok sound-off hooks, tips, founder clips

elements.title: Pop-In Overshoot
elements.desc: Spring pop wrapper (scale overshoot) with configurable preset.
elements.use: chips, icons, stickers, cards entering.

elements.title: Poster Callout Lines
elements.desc: Poster cover with the hero shifted onto its own paper colour, many short phrases in empty paper, and fine curves drawing on as callouts and sweeps
elements.use: editorial poster/cover with a group or multiple-exposure hero and annotation-style phrases

elements.title: Print Texture Transitions
elements.desc: Ink-bleed reveal - the next scene soaks in through a feathery, turbulence-displaced circular mask that wobbles outward from an ink drop, with a dark wet edge ahead of it.
elements.use: paper and ink aesthetics, narrative or writerly scene changes.

elements.title: Process Flow Steps
elements.desc: Numbered steps joined by a connector that draws down between them; node lands, line draws, next node lands. Use for a sequence the viewer should feel as an order.
elements.use: how-it-works, 3-5 ordered steps, a workflow or recipe.

elements.title: Product Card Progressive Assemble
elements.desc: A product card is filled in field by field like a form - a fill-cursor box hops between fields, skeleton bars give way to content, the price is downgraded with a strike-through and a new price springs in, marker highlights sweep the copy and the button fills last.
elements.use: product detail cards, pricing changes, "the information structure of this card" walk-throughs.

elements.title: Product Turntable
elements.desc: Procedural lathe bottle with a generated label texture on a turntable in a studio cyclorama, two lights, slow 360 with a hero hold. Label text is a prop. Use for product hero shots.
elements.use: product hero/reveal shots, packaging showcases (swap label text/colours).

elements.title: Progress Bar Line
elements.desc: Full-width bar along the bottom (or top) that grows linearly with the frame.
elements.use: Any reel/long scene: subtle global progress, countdowns, timers.

elements.title: Prop Barrel 3D
elements.desc: Lathe-profile barrel with metal hoops that rolls in, wobbles to a stop and rotates slowly; matte wood and steel.
elements.use: game/industrial/pirate beats, 3D inserts.

elements.title: Prop Crate 3D
elements.desc: Procedural wooden crate (slats, corner braces) that drops in with a squash bounce and turns slowly under a 3/4 camera on a studio floor.
elements.use: game/adventure/product-logistics reels, 3D prop inserts.

elements.title: Prop Lantern 3D
elements.desc: Paper-style lantern with a glowing core, point light and seeded flicker; sways gently from a hook with a warm halo on the floor.
elements.use: night/ambient/horror/festival beats, warm accent insert.

elements.title: Pulse Orb
elements.desc: Glowing core with expanding ripple rings; ring strength and core size follow the audio level.
elements.use: AI-assistant/voice/music reels: listening, speaking and thinking beats.

elements.title: Punctuation Zoom
elements.desc: The sentence's own full stop is the shared element: the camera pans onto it and dives exponentially (up to 72x) until the dot fills the frame and becomes the next scene, where a glyph tile bursts out a tilted picture card. Use for chapter changes and "and then..." reveals.
elements.use: chapter/section changes, punchline-to-scene reveals, "the full stop becomes the next shot".

elements.title: Push-In Camera
elements.desc: Damped virtual-camera push-in/pan with optional handheld drift applied to children.
elements.use: cinematic emphasis on a card/subject.

elements.title: Push Transition
elements.desc: Scene B shoves scene A off-frame in one eased move; A darkens, B lands from slightly oversize, and a shadow rides the seam. Use for clean sequential scene changes.
elements.use: chapters, before/after, step-by-step edits.

elements.title: Pyramid Tiers
elements.desc: Stacked trapezoid tiers that build bottom-up, apex lit in the accent colour, each with a label and a note. Use when the sentence is about levels or a funnel.
elements.use: a hierarchy or funnel (many at the bottom, few at the top), levels of skill, tiers of a product.

elements.title: Quad Split Parallel Scenes
elements.desc: Quad-split montage: four micro-scenes (browser, terminal, word drops, approval flow) run in parallel with hard cuts and no transitions, with their key beats staggered 3-6 frames apart, then hold on the finished states. Use for a dense "many things happening at once" montage beat.
elements.use: a feature-dense montage where several things happen together, the midpoint density peak of a trailer or promo, a background-track chorus.

elements.title: Radial Ripple Phone Chips
elements.desc: A quiet product hero on a warm sand ground: four out-of-phase concentric circles breathe like ripples, a phone rises to the centre with an auto-scrolling feed, and two white feature chips pop in one after another and hover.
elements.use: the "this is it" hold for a mobile product; a product-overview beat where feature names sit either side of the device; a title or end card with the product in view.

elements.title: Radial Wave
elements.desc: A dot grid is switched on by a wave from the centre (each dot overshoots to 1.5x mid-travel and settles lit), then a faster outside-in glow pulse answers; the grid stays lit as a base for the next beat.
elements.use: "power on" moments, scale of a network or user base, a textured backdrop that wakes up.

elements.title: Ranked Bar Race
elements.desc: Horizontal bars re-sort by value with rolling counters; rank is a continuous crossing so rows swap exactly where values cross. Use for leaderboards and period-over-period rankings.
elements.use: leaderboards, weekly rankings, market share races.

elements.title: Ransom Note Title
elements.desc: Title built from mismatched cut-out letters (different fonts, colours, tilts) that slap in one by one; collage/scrapbook headline.
elements.use: quirky or true-crime-style titles, collage reels.

elements.title: Reel Cover Seam
elements.desc: 9:16 cover with a top and bottom image joined by a Ben-Day dot seam and big "10 -> 40" text kept inside the IG grid 3:4 crop
elements.use: before/after or age-A to age-B reel covers, publish-package thumbnails

elements.title: Region Map Highlight
elements.desc: Filled SVG map where the camera zooms to a target region, it fills with the accent while others dim, location markers drop in with pulses, then a stat callout.
elements.use: "an animated map of X", regional stat reveal, store/office/coverage spotlight, geographic transition.

elements.title: Research Card Stack Scroll
elements.desc: A research pipeline - one card drops in per beat, then sinks down-right while blurring and dimming over three beats before being recycled; only the newest card shows its body and a background grid scrolls at exactly the stack speed.
elements.use: throughput and volume statements: sources read, documents processed, research feeds.

elements.title: Rhythm Interrupt Moves
elements.desc: Three hard zoom jumps (1.0, 1.6, 2.6) pinned to one target card with a brightness tick on each jump, no tween between steps. Use to force focus on one metric by breaking continuity on purpose.
elements.use: forcing attention onto one metric or card in a dashboard-like layout; documentary "watch this" beats; a deliberate break in a continuous shot.

elements.title: Ring Progress KPI
elements.desc: Donut KPI ring that fills to value/max with a counting centre number.
elements.use: single-metric callouts (completion, score, uptime).

elements.title: Ring Waveform
elements.desc: 72 radial bars around a circle reading the energy track at staggered delays ((i%24)*2 frames), alternating two colours.
elements.use: beat-synced / lyric reels needing this piece.

elements.title: Riso Halftone Plates
elements.desc: Two or three spot-ink plates built from halftone dots, multiply-blended on warm paper with 2-4px misregistration, stepping at 12fps
elements.use: indie/zine/event-poster looks, a printed hero backdrop behind type.

elements.title: Riso Misregistration Hit
elements.desc: A poster headline slams in, splits into two multiply-blended riso ink plates that shake out of register, then hard-cuts to perfect registration with a stamp and a scale pulse. Use for one emphatic hit on a print-style headline.
elements.use: a paper/zine/poster look needs one emphatic hit on a headline, once or twice per film.

elements.title: Rocket Launch 3D
elements.desc: Stylised two-part rocket (body, cone, fins) with an engine plume that lifts off with smoke puffs while the camera tilts up to follow.
elements.use: space/launch/news reels, countdown payoffs.

elements.title: Route Map Card
elements.desc: Rounded map card with stops at normalised positions, dashed route drawing up to the current stop, a ring gliding between stops, only the current stop labelled
elements.use: walk/trip reels showing progress between places (pair with `location-pill`)

elements.title: Row Embed
elements.desc: Rows are not shown, they are grown into the page - each drops from the air in an accelerating beat with rotateX flattening, a slot patch and dashed slot frame underneath, a 2 px accent seam opening along its bottom edge on impact, while the camera pans down.
elements.use: detail pages, spec lists and forms whose rows should "click" into a layout.

elements.title: Running List
elements.desc: A list that stays on screen while the speaker works through it; each item arrives on the frame it is spoken and the newest is lit. Use over a talking head for "three things" scripts.
elements.use: a speaker names 3-4 things over several seconds; cutting away per item loses the thread, showing all up front spoils the reveal.

elements.title: Sakuga Button Hit
elements.desc: Big button gets pressed twice: squash and overshoot, an ink impact frame, a burst, tick fan and a sound word; anime-style tap reaction.
elements.use: tap or CTA beats, "press here" moments.

elements.title: Sakuga Checkbox Tick
elements.desc: Checkbox is ticked with a slash swing, glints and a ring, then unticks by shrinking the mark; squash keeps volume.
elements.use: done, agree, task-complete beats.

elements.title: Sakuga Input Typing
elements.desc: Text field gets focus with wobble marks, each typed letter kicks a small smoke puff, and Enter lands a burst and a ping word.
elements.use: search, sign-up, typing-in-a-field beats.

elements.title: Sakuga Progress Fill
elements.desc: Progress bar fills with a storm cloud rolling on its leading edge, then completes with a burst, a smoke ring and a done word.
elements.use: loading, upload, goal-reached beats.

elements.title: Sakuga Radio Select
elements.desc: Three radio options: the selection jumps down the list, the new dot pops with squash and a tick fan while the old one shrinks away.
elements.use: pick-one choices, plan or option selection.

elements.title: Sakuga Rating Stars
elements.desc: Five stars fill one after another, each popping with squash and a glint; the last one throws shards and a burst.
elements.use: reviews, scores, five-star moments.

elements.title: Sakuga Slider Drag
elements.desc: Slider knob is dragged fast and leaves rolling cumulus clouds, then snaps back with squash; value pops in a bubble.
elements.use: amount, volume, intensity changes.

elements.title: Sakuga Tabs Switch
elements.desc: Three tabs: the active indicator whips to the next tab with a smear and speed lines, the tab squashes, and the content card swaps with a pop.
elements.use: section switching, menu or category changes.

elements.title: Sakuga Timing Shift
elements.desc: A cel card flips up the frame on threes (one drawing every 3 source frames, labelled ON 3s), then a single impact frame and a one-frame-per-drawing sprint back to centre with squash on landing. Use for a hand-drawn to full-motion contrast on a single element.
elements.use: emphasis moves on a single element (a card entering, a metric landing); you want the contrast of "hand-held cadence, then a rush".

elements.title: Sakuga Toast Drop
elements.desc: Notification card smears in from the side, lands with dust puffs and a squash, shows a message, then leaves by shrinking.
elements.use: notifications, alerts, "saved" confirmations.

elements.title: Sakuga Toggle Flip
elements.desc: Switch flips on and off with a stretched, smeared knob, splash chips, a ring and a click word; procedural, no painted frames.
elements.use: on/off, enable, dark-mode style beats.

elements.title: Sakuga Tooltip Pop
elements.desc: Info button gets hovered: a speech-bubble tooltip springs out with overshoot, wobble marks and tick fan, then shrinks away.
elements.use: hints, tips, "did you know" callouts.

elements.title: Satellite Swarm Globe
elements.desc: Dotted globe with a seeded swarm of satellites on tilted circular orbits; each leaves a short trail, orbits fade in one by one.
elements.use: space, telecom, connectivity and "global network" reels.

elements.title: Scan Bracket Sweep
elements.desc: A document pops in and stays still while four L-shaped corner brackets land on it and a scan band with a velocity tail sweeps it back and forth. Use for a "reading or validating this content" process shot.
elements.use: a "parsing or checking this document" process shot, or a document-product capability demo.

elements.title: Scanline Annotate Focus
elements.desc: A strictly linear scan line crosses an existing page; each block it passes gets four corner brackets that spring in, a typed machine label and a live counter. Use for "AI is reading this page or brand" analysis shots.
elements.use: an "AI is reading your page or brand" analysis shot, a design-system or brand-guide breakdown, or a self-description beat for a product.

elements.title: Scanline Assemble Flyin
elements.desc: A blueprint artboard of dashed slots; a linear scan line crosses it and each component flies in from off-screen with an overshoot, a directional smear and snapping corner marks, finishing as the scan ends. Use for a page-generation opener.
elements.use: a "page builds itself" opener, an AI site-builder or auto-layout product demo, or a blank-to-finished narrative.

elements.title: Scene Edge Transition
elements.desc: Wrapper that warps or whips a scene in over its first 8 src frames and out over its last 8 (Warp/Whip from impact).
elements.use: Fast cuts between scenes in a reel; wrap each scene in its own Sequence.

elements.title: Scoreboard Compare
elements.desc: Two-column scoreboard (A vs B) with rows that count up and a winner tick on the higher side; for flight/version/season comparisons.
elements.use: this-vs-last comparisons (version 15 vs 14, before vs after).

elements.title: Scramble Decode
elements.desc: Left-to-right glyph scramble that resolves into the real text (hacker/decode reveal).
elements.use: tech/cyber reveals, labels, codes

elements.title: Scribble Circle Word
elements.desc: A hand-drawn marker circle (wobbly, overshooting loop) draws itself around a word or phrase; seeded wobble so it is identical every render.
elements.use: pointing at a key word, "this one" callouts.

elements.title: Scroll Brake Moves
elements.desc: Long-list brake: a tall changelog-style list flies past, slows with a long tail and stops on the target row, which lifts while the others dim; the reticle variant adds a hard overshooting brake and four corner brackets snapping on the same frame. Use for release histories, changelogs and "the latest one is the biggest".
elements.use: a changelog, release history or long list runs past at speed and stops on one entry that matters ("we keep shipping, and this one is the biggest"). Use `reticle-lock` when the stop needs more punch.

elements.title: Segmented Thumb Hero
elements.desc: An oversized two-option segmented control as the whole shot: it springs in, an outlined cursor slides in and presses, the white thumb slides to the other segment, and the new icon pops while the old one collapses. Use to announce a mode switch.
elements.use: announcing a 'mode switch' or A/B choice feature; a single UI micro-interaction carrying a whole close-up shot.

elements.title: Selection Gizmo Box
elements.desc: Editor-style selection: pointer click selects an object, bounding box with 8 handles + rotate knob + axis arrows, drag to move, corner-drag to scale with live X/Y/scale readout, then swap the object.
elements.use: "edit the scene yourself" beats, cut-out/product swap demos, editor tutorials.

elements.title: Shape Morph Sequence
elements.desc: One SVG path morphs through a list of shapes via per-point interpolation; includes resamplePath helper
elements.use: brand stories, topic transitions, music visuals that transform instead of cut

elements.title: Shot Transitions
elements.desc: Three ways to hand one shot to the next - a flash-cut (push-in with a white flash over the cut), a whip-pan that swaps scenes inside heavy horizontal blur, and a portal wipe where a card in the first scene grows into a full-screen window onto the second.
elements.use: any two-shot seam: flash-cut for even-energy page-to-page seams, whip-pan for fast feature runs, portal wipe for "open this card to enter its world".

elements.title: Shutter Close
elements.desc: Two black bars close from top and bottom (or left and right) with ease-in cubic, scene swaps under the closed shutter, then optionally reopens
elements.use: a hard "snap" cut between scenes or onto an end card.

elements.title: Side Lyric Words
elements.desc: Red lyric words either side of a subject's face on the eye line, pairs pop on beat with overshoot and hold to the next pair
elements.use: lyric/hook words beside a talking-head or portrait, synced to a BPM.

elements.title: Silhouette Text Outline
elements.desc: A word repeated along a closed outline path around a subject, scrolling continuously (SVG textPath startOffset loop)
elements.use: a subject cut-out with a repeating word ("LOVE", "WOW") hugging its outline.

elements.title: Siri Wave Line
elements.desc: Three overlapping sine waves with a bell envelope and a pink-to-cyan gradient; amplitude surges with the audio level.
elements.use: AI-assistant/voice/music reels: listening, speaking and thinking beats.

elements.title: Slam Entrance Moves
elements.desc: Three high-energy slam entrances in one element: a perspective whip-in (snap-whip), a score card dropped from the lens (score-slam), and an impact burst that pushes neighbouring cards (impact-burst). Use for a hero or KPI card entrance that must read as impact.
elements.use: a hero or KPI card needs a heavy entrance that reads as impact, one slam per film.

elements.title: Slice Transition
elements.desc: Scene A is cut into slanted bands that slide out alternately left and right, center-out, to uncover scene B. Use for punchy scene changes.
elements.use: beat-synced scene cuts, energetic reels.

elements.title: Slot Refill Ticker
elements.desc: Lanes advance on one discrete step clock; a finished lane fills, its job icon exits right, and the next tick a new job takes the same lane. Use for queue, scheduler and throughput visuals.
elements.use: queues, schedulers, token or job throughput.

elements.title: Sonar Sweep Reveal
elements.desc: A clockwise sector beam sweeps a fixed pivot; the scene is clear inside the beam and dimmed behind a dark LED aperture grid outside it. Use for scan, radar or reveal moments.
elements.use: scan/radar/detect reveals, hero image unveils, tech intros.

elements.title: Sound Design Panel
elements.desc: Seeded waveform bar strip with a sweeping playhead, a cues.json code panel fading in line by line, and popping pills.
elements.use: Explaining audio/sound design, 'how it is built' panels, config/code call-outs.

elements.title: Space Camera Moves
elements.desc: Page treated as a 3D object in two variants. exploded = parts lift along Z in isometric view, hover with numbered callouts, then reassemble with a thud; dive = drone dive from near-vertical down onto a hero card (82/18 speed split, cushion landing). Use for big highlight beats, at most twice per film.
elements.use: architecture / "what is it made of" (exploded) or opening that smashes from the global map into the hero (dive).

elements.title: Spark Burst
elements.desc: Seeded radial particles with drag, gravity, shrink and fade; closed-form positions.
elements.use: celebration, impact, success moments.

elements.title: Sparkline Ticker
elements.desc: Smooth sparkline that draws left to right with a glowing end dot, a live value readout following the dot and a soft area fill.
elements.use: trend/price/engagement lines in a card or lower third.

elements.title: Speed Ramp Cut
elements.desc: Signature hard cut plus speed ramp: content is already visible and at peak velocity on frame 0, then a power4-out settle over 72 frames with no overshoot, with motion blur on the fast part. Exports speedRamp, speedRampStyle, RampCut and RampBlur. Use as the transition between every beat.
elements.use: every beat boundary of a white-ground explainer or product short; one dominant property per cut (scale, x/y or a small rotate).

elements.title: Speed Ramp Freeze
elements.desc: Frame remap that stops a flowing card rail dead on one card (a pause, viewfinder brackets and a PAUSED timecode), circles it with a marker stroke and a note, then thaws with a smootherstep that covers one card pitch. Use to hold a reader on one item in a fast list.
elements.use: a fast card list or long scroll must stop on one item to be read (review, teaching, "this one first").

elements.title: Speed Streaks
elements.desc: Anime speed lines: tapered white wedges rushing in from the edges toward a clear oval around the subject, re-seeded every 2 source frames
elements.use: spins, whip moves, impact shots on a subject.

elements.title: Splash Rings Word
elements.desc: Three staggered elliptical rings expand and fade while a big italic word drops from above on a damped spring.
elements.use: beat-synced / lyric reels needing this piece.

elements.title: Split Screen Slide
elements.desc: Two stacked halves slide in from opposite sides (expo ease, 3-frame offset) with captions and a pill between; then three vertical columns drop in and cycle content on the beat. Use for A/B looks or multi-shot montage transitions.
elements.use: comparisons, before/after-style intros, montage beats.

elements.title: Spoken Word Caption
elements.desc: Words light up as spoken (current word highlighted, past 100%, upcoming 50%), fading in and out around the line. Takes [text, startSec, endSec] triples.
elements.use: a single spoken line with word-level timing inside a scene.

elements.title: Spotlight Hero Card
elements.desc: A warm spotlight wanders over a page of cards in a dark room, locks on one hero card, pushes the camera into a slanted close-up, then the card rises, hovers, lands again with a champagne outline sweeping its edge and a 3D annotation beside it. Use for a single-hero product opening.
elements.use: a single-hero product opening where one object (a card, item or module) must read as the atomic unit of the product; slow, premium openers.

elements.title: Spotlight Sweep Moves
elements.desc: Dark-stage spotlight as camera and edit. A linear spot wakes a UI panel as it sweeps across and lets it sleep again (wake-sleep), a purple edge light rounds a corner while the panel slides under it (edge-pan), or a linear radial spot grows from the top-left corner until everything is lit (corner-reveal). Use for dark brand films that introduce UI panels one by one, or as a light-driven transition between sections.
elements.use: dark-tone brand films introducing UI panels or feature areas one at a time; a black-stage opening that lights the interface up; light-driven transitions between sections.

elements.title: Stacked Half Panels
elements.desc: Two 940x580 cards stacked for 9:16, slid in from opposite sides and linked by one playhead sweeping both: top is the outline, bottom fills in behind the playhead.
elements.use: plan-to-result, before/after, prompt-to-output, any "this becomes that" beat for vertical video.

elements.title: Stage Split Timeline
elements.desc: Vertical mission timeline where one track splits into two lanes at a chosen event; time-code ticks, labelled milestones and a moving cursor.
elements.use: launch/process timelines with a split (staging, fork, parallel tracks).

elements.title: Stamp Slam
elements.desc: Rubber-stamp text scaling 3->1 rotated -14deg with a red border and multiply blend, with impact shake and flash.
elements.use: verdicts, approvals/rejections, "no refunds" punchlines over documents or footage.

elements.title: Starburst Rays
elements.desc: Rotating rays from a centre point, plus a comic spiky white pop variant, both kicking on the beat
elements.use: reaction/pop moments behind a face or product, beat-synced.

elements.title: Statement Takeover
elements.desc: Footage dims under a scrim and one claim owns the frame; words land one by one with one accented word and a slow drift. Use for the single strongest line of a video.
elements.use: the one line that must land (a thesis, a claim, the hook payoff).

elements.title: Status Log Feed
elements.desc: Terminal-style mission log: timestamped lines type in one by one with coloured status tags (OK, WARN, FAIL) and a blinking cursor.
elements.use: mission/ops/launch logs, "system report" beats.

elements.title: Steep Tilt Glide
elements.desc: Fixed camera on a 60-degree wall of UI blocks; the page itself slides sideways across the frame with speed ghosts while its blocks hover and land one by one. Use for long multi-section UI tours in a dark, neon tone.
elements.use: a long multi-block product page or dashboard is toured in one shot, dark neon tone, content should read as passing a still camera. Pick it over a camera-move card in the same segment (graze-face-tour moves the camera and keeps the page still; this one does the reverse).

elements.title: Step Card Modal
elements.desc: White window card with traffic-light dots, STEP pill, heavy title and staggered arrow parameter lines; springs in from below.
elements.use: Explaining a technique/step over footage, how-to reels, feature call-outs.

elements.title: Sticker Arrow Callout
elements.desc: Die-cut stickers (14-point WOW burst, heart, round NEW badge) pop on beats with a white cut stroke, then a thick hand-drawn arrow draws on with a this-one tag and three sparkles. Use for playful callouts.
elements.use: social callouts, playful highlight of one thing.

elements.title: Stickman Celebrate
elements.desc: Stickman jumps with both arms up while seeded confetti and sparkles burst; win, launch or milestone beat.
elements.use: wins, milestones, "we did it".

elements.title: Stickman Facepalm Fail
elements.desc: Stickman slumps into a facepalm after a FAIL stamp slams in; mistake or failure beat.
elements.use: mistakes, "what not to do", bad outcomes.

elements.title: Stickman Laptop Work
elements.desc: Stickman types at a laptop on a desk; a stream of small blocks pops from the screen; work, coding or research beat.
elements.use: working, building, researching.

elements.title: Stickman Money Rain
elements.desc: Coins rain down around a smug stickman with arms out catching them; income, profit and "worth it" beat.
elements.use: earnings, savings, price reveals.

elements.title: Stickman Phone Scroll
elements.desc: Tired stickman scrolls a phone while notification bubbles pop around; doomscrolling, distraction or procrastination beat.
elements.use: distraction, screen time, "I should be working".

elements.title: Stickman Point Board
elements.desc: Stickman points at a board that reveals three bullet lines one by one; explainer "here are the three things".
elements.use: lists, steps, three-point explainers.

elements.title: Stickman Run Dash
elements.desc: Fast run with leaning body, speed lines and dust puffs; urgency, escape or "rush" beat.
elements.use: deadlines, chases, hurry.

elements.title: Stickman Shrug Question
elements.desc: Stickman shrugs with a puzzled face and floating question marks; confusion, "who knows", unanswered question beat.
elements.use: rhetorical questions, "nobody knows", doubt.

elements.title: Stickman Surprise Jump
elements.desc: Stickman recoils with a shock jump, wide eyes and a big exclamation mark with a camera shake; plot twist beat.
elements.use: plot twists, shocking facts, reveals.

elements.title: Stickman Think Idea
elements.desc: Stickman ponders with question marks, then a light bulb switches on with rays and a happy jump.
elements.use: idea moments, "what if", solutions after a problem.

elements.title: Stickman Thumbs-Up Outro
elements.desc: Stickman gives a thumbs-up, winks and a heart pops; friendly closing beat with a follow/subscribe caption.
elements.use: video endings, calls to action.

elements.title: Stickman Two Talk
elements.desc: Two stickmen face each other and trade three speech bubbles; dialogue, objection-and-answer or Q&A beat.
elements.use: conversation, myth vs fact, questions and answers.

elements.title: Stickman Walk Cycle
elements.desc: Looping stickman walk across the frame on a ground line; stride phase is locked to travel speed so feet do not slide.
elements.use: travel beats, "then I went to...", transitions between scenes.

elements.title: Stickman Wave Intro
elements.desc: Stickman hops in, waves with a speech bubble and a one-line caption; friendly opener for explainer reels.
elements.use: channel or explainer opening, greeting.

elements.title: Stickman v2 Expression Sheet
elements.desc: Still reference sheet of 10 face expressions (neutral, worried, scared, shock, smirk, angry, sad, grin, tired, laugh) on the round white head with beanie.
elements.use: face reference, expression picking, rig QA.

elements.title: Stickman v2 Hand Sheet
elements.desc: Still reference sheet of the five finger-drawn hand shapes (relaxed, open, fist, point, grip), shown large with the sleeve, plus a left and a right.
elements.use: hand reference, rig QA.

elements.title: Stickman v2 Pose Sheet
elements.desc: Still reference sheet of 12 poses in the boxy line-art style (outlined box torso, thin limbs, round feet).
elements.use: character reference, pose picking, rig QA.

elements.title: Stickman v2 Survival Thriller
elements.desc: Sample scene in the new stickman look: round white head, expressive face, white gloves, hard ceiling light and a crescent shade on the face; a night-shift dispatcher takes a call, panics, and a silhouette appears in the doorway before the lights cut and a rule card lands.
elements.use: suspense openers, urban-legend and survival-rule shorts, cold-open hooks.

elements.title: Strike Replace Word
elements.desc: Old word gets a red strike-through line drawn across it, fades up, and the new word drops in below in the accent colour.
elements.use: corrections, "not X, Y" hooks, before/after wording.

elements.title: Stroke Segment Build
elements.desc: A word is built from sixteen disconnected neon tube segments that ignite in scrambled order; it stays unreadable for most of the shot until the last three key strokes land, the sign flares and the word suddenly reads. Use for a delayed-meaning reveal of a short brand word.
elements.use: a short, recognisable word or product name that is revealed with a suspense beat; one per piece.

elements.title: Subscribe CTA
elements.desc: Follow/Subscribe button: pop-in, press, ripple, state change to 'Following' with check and bell wiggle.
elements.use: social CTAs at the end of a reel; generic, no brand logos.

elements.title: SVG Stroke Draw-On
elements.desc: Draw-on any SVG path via strokeDashoffset using the pathLength=1 trick (no getTotalLength).
elements.use: logos, checkmarks, underlines, line-art reveals, signatures.

elements.title: Swipe Card Carousel
elements.desc: A phone-style card carousel with one owner of track position: a visible finger drags (linear), release snaps (decelerate), a next-button press advances, a last swipe lands. Focused card scales up, neighbours dim; two cards carry the owner headshots via SubjectFill.
elements.use: app/feature walkthroughs, step-by-step cards, onboarding swipes.

elements.title: Swiss Grid Type
elements.desc: 12-column grid with type that wipes into cells on one snap curve; one signal colour, hard-cut deletions.
elements.use: brand/event/conference openers, identity titles

elements.title: Tape Torn Card
elements.desc: Paper card with a torn bottom edge, two translucent tape strips and a slight tilt that drops in with a settle; scrapbook/collage card for a headline or fact.
elements.use: collage reels, fact cards, news-style callouts over footage.

elements.title: Tear Streak Transitions
elements.desc: Glitch displace - the page is cut into 16 uneven horizontal strips that jitter sideways with two-colour ghosts and scanlines; the hard cut to the next page happens inside the peak of the tear and the strips settle back.
elements.use: high-energy page changes with a digital-glitch meaning, state jumps (rolling out to live).

elements.title: Tension Camera Moves
elements.desc: Two emotional camera moves for a single tense beat. Bullet-time freeze orbit (content stops mid-growth, sparks hang in the air, the camera swings 52 degrees around a live chart and back) or pull-back isolation (a close-up metric pulls back while sibling cards go dark one by one until the hero stands alone). Use for a peak moment or a closing beat, not both in one shot.
elements.use: a peak or freeze-frame moment on a core number or chart; a closing "only this matters" beat.

elements.title: Terminal 3D
elements.desc: Three terminal windows float in 3D space. The camera flies window to window, pulls back mid-flight to show all three, and at each stop a typewriter types a command while its output prints line by line, ending on a lime READY line. Use for a CLI or developer workflow shown as a three-step spatial journey.
elements.use: CLI or developer-tool demos where a three-step command sequence should read as three places; "install, build, ship" flows.

elements.title: Terminal Insert
elements.desc: Flat, glow-free CLI window with traffic-light chrome that settles in with a perspective tilt, types a command, shows a big flat terminal word, streams "◇ ... ✓" rows and finishes on a success line with a blinking block cursor. Use for installs, agent runs and "one command" proof.
elements.use: CLI/install/agent-run beats, "one command does it" proof, dev-tool explainers.

elements.title: Text As Mask
elements.desc: Huge block letters act as a window: inside the strokes a slowly drifting dark KPI panel shows through; after an inhale the letterforms push in far past the frame and the panel takes over the whole screen. Use for a brand word or slogan that opens into the product visual.
elements.use: a brand word or slogan that should introduce a product screen in the same frame; a chapter card where the letters are a door and the product sits behind them.

elements.title: Text Column Converge
elements.desc: Two words pinned at equal edge margins hard-cut through a list, then a single ease-in-out slide converges them into one phrase at the end; use for a closing reveal of a product name after a feature list.
elements.use: a recap or outro that runs a feature list and then reveals the product name or tagline in one move.

elements.title: Theme Switch Moves
elements.desc: Two dark-mode switch moves on one UI: a day/night toggle press followed by a 15 degree dusk line that re-skins the whole screen in place (sweep), or a command palette that types 'dark', collapses CRT-style to a dot and ripples the dark theme out from it (ripple).
elements.use: dark-mode or theme feature segments where the same UI visibly changes colour in front of the viewer instead of cutting to a new scene.

elements.title: Thinking Braid
elements.desc: Three dotted strands plaiting around each other down a column; a "weaving" state.
elements.use: AI-agent status beats: thinking, searching, using tools; loaders for AI explainer reels.

elements.title: Thinking Breathing Ring
elements.desc: Ring of dots that slowly breathes in and out and morphs radius with a travelling wave; calm "thinking" state.
elements.use: AI-agent status beats: thinking, searching, using tools; loaders for AI explainer reels.

elements.title: Thinking Constellation Web
elements.desc: Seeded star nodes that wire themselves up with lines one by one, then pulse; a "connecting" state.
elements.use: AI-agent status beats: thinking, searching, using tools; loaders for AI explainer reels.

elements.title: Thinking Dot Morph
elements.desc: Dotted outline that morphs circle, triangle, square, circle in a loop; dots slide along the path.
elements.use: AI-agent status beats: thinking, searching, using tools; loaders for AI explainer reels.

elements.title: Thinking Orb Idle
elements.desc: Dot-lattice sphere that spins slowly (6.5 s per turn); near dots larger and brighter, far dots fade.
elements.use: AI-agent status beats: thinking, searching, using tools; loaders for AI explainer reels.

elements.title: Thinking Orb Reasoning
elements.desc: Dot sphere where a single lit dot hops between dots every 220 ms leaving a fading seven-dot tail.
elements.use: AI-agent status beats: thinking, searching, using tools; loaders for AI explainer reels.

elements.title: Thinking Orb Searching
elements.desc: Dot sphere with a lens spot that hops between five places on the front face every 1.8 s, lighting the dots under it.
elements.use: AI-agent status beats: thinking, searching, using tools; loaders for AI explainer reels.

elements.title: Thinking Orb Waiting
elements.desc: Dot sphere with a comet of light circling the equator every 2 s while the sphere turns slowly.
elements.use: AI-agent status beats: thinking, searching, using tools; loaders for AI explainer reels.

elements.title: Thinking Orb Working
elements.desc: Dot sphere spinning faster (3 s per turn) while a band of light runs down it every 1.7 s.
elements.use: AI-agent status beats: thinking, searching, using tools; loaders for AI explainer reels.

elements.title: Thinking Orbit Particles
elements.desc: Particles circling on tilted orbits around a faint core (the "working" look of an agent).
elements.use: AI-agent status beats: thinking, searching, using tools; loaders for AI explainer reels.

elements.title: Time Pill Buzz
elements.desc: Clock-icon pill that fades in, buzzes like a phone vibration, holds, then rises and fades out (2 s); use for timestamps between scenes
elements.use: labelling a scene change ("7 AM") or a timeline of a day.

elements.title: Timeline Travel
elements.desc: A sideways timeline trip: the camera accelerates along a version axis, each version card springs up as the camera passes its tick, and the last tick is reached with a hard brake and a push-in. Use for changelogs, milestones and product-history beats.
elements.use: changelog, milestone or product-history sections; a "we kept shipping" beat told as a horizontal trip. Pairs with scroll-brake-moves (vertical list brake); this one is horizontal travel.

elements.title: Title Behind Subject
elements.desc: Big white title layered between background and a foreground subject cutout, soft-in with blur sharpening, hold, fade
elements.use: portrait/product with a depth-sandwich title (subject cutout overlaps the letters).

elements.title: Title Demote To Label
elements.desc: A headline stands as the hero, then one continuous tween shrinks it into a top-left section label while content grows underneath; use for chapter openers and section handoffs.
elements.use: chapter openers where the title should stay on screen as the section label after the content arrives.

elements.title: Torn Paper Wipe
elements.desc: Transition: a ragged torn-paper edge sweeps across the frame revealing the next scene; paper strip stays visible along the tear.
elements.use: collage/scrapbook cuts between scenes.

elements.title: Torus Knot 3D
elements.desc: Glossy torus knot that spins and slowly shifts hue under two coloured lights; abstract hero object for tech and product reels.
elements.use: abstract title backdrops, tech/product hero, loop bumpers.

elements.title: Trailer Grammar Moves
elements.desc: Trailer cold open: three 18 f hard cuts (two full views and a 2.2x punch on one card), a pure-black beat, then a title card whose tracking settles from wide to tight before a frozen hold. Use as the first 4-5 s of a promo, before the main title.
elements.use: the open of a trailer or promo: three fast punchy shots, a silent beat, then the title.

elements.title: Transition Hidden Cut
elements.desc: Three ways to hide a hard cut inside 1-3 frames of distraction - a soft foreground object sweeping the lens, a collision with flash/shake/stamp, or a warm light leak that peaks as the scene swaps.
elements.use: seamless "one take" changes (invisible-cut), versus openers (versus-slam), warm film-style chapter changes (light-leak-burn).

elements.title: Transition Travel
elements.desc: Letterform zoom - a giant title built from block letters is a window onto the next scene; the camera dives into the stem of the letter I until the hole swallows the frame and the leftover cover is thrown away.
elements.use: chapter title to content where the title should be the door; high-energy replacement for a chapter card.

elements.title: Trash Bin Drop
elements.desc: Three generic app tiles arc in from the left, spin and shrink into a trash bin that punches on every hit while their labels get struck through - the "you don't need X" hook. Use to dismiss tools, steps or old habits.
elements.use: "you don't need ..." hooks, tool-replacement pitches, decluttering/before-after set-ups.

elements.title: Tunnel Flythrough 3D
elements.desc: Camera flies down a tunnel of glowing rings that streak past, with a slight sway and colour shift along depth.
elements.use: transitions, "enter the system" and speed beats.

elements.title: Twinkle Stars
elements.desc: Field of staggered twinkling 4-point stars at given positions (sin^2 scale, spinning), each twinkles twice.
elements.use: sparkle accents over gold/hero text or on dark backgrounds

elements.title: Type and Filter
elements.desc: On a real-looking UI, a query is typed character by character, the camera closes on the search box and then pulls back, the other cards leave in reading order until one card remains, that card slides to the first slot, and a double ripple click pushes the camera into it. Use for the "do the action" beat of a feature demo: search, filter, open a detail view.
elements.use: feature demos where the viewer should follow a human-paced action: search, filter, open an item; a single interaction beat after a high-energy section.

elements.title: Type Assembly Moves
elements.desc: Three title-assembly variants: letters rise from a clip line (split), drift in blurred and lock into place (drift), or ride a rising arc and lift into the title (path); use for headline and tagline entrances.
elements.use: headline or tagline entrances where the route the letters take carries meaning: split as the neutral default, drift for a brand-name reveal, path for a sentence riding a rising line or graph.

elements.title: Letter Drop Physics
elements.desc: Letters fall from above on gravity, bounce twice with decaying height, land skewed by a seeded tilt, then all stand upright together; use for playful opening titles.
elements.use: light-tone opening titles and card headlines where a bit of physical comedy suits the tone.

elements.title: Type Rhythm Sync
elements.desc: Headline words pulse with a beat (pump mode thickens the strokes on each hit and settles back, with a step sequencer lighting in time) or fill left to right as narration reads them (karaoke mode). Use for beat- or voice-locked headlines, not silent text.
elements.use: a headline locked to a music bed (pump) or to a read-aloud line (karaoke); high-energy beats where the type acts as the bass drum.

elements.title: Typewriter Error Retype
elements.desc: A typewriter types a bland phrase, hesitates with a blinking caret, backspaces it away and retypes the real line faster. The three speed tiers carry the drama. Use for slogans and negation-then-statement copy, not for long text.
elements.use: a slogan card where the copy changes its mind ("just a slideshow" becomes "your cinematic crew"); negation-then-statement copy.

elements.title: Typewriter (zero-reflow caret)
elements.desc: Typed text with a caret that never shifts layout; for product input boxes and prompts. Variants: atxt-19-typewriter.
elements.use: typing inside an input/prompt box, terminal lines

elements.title: UI Strip Away Outro
elements.desc: A subtractive ending - after clicking Publish the whole editor UI evaporates layer by layer from the outside in, starting with the left sidebar rail, until only the button is left; it slides to the centre and grows, fades out and hands the black stage to the wordmark.
elements.use: publish / done endings, "one click and the complexity is gone".

elements.title: UI To Brand Morph
elements.desc: The UI becomes the brand. icon-flip-bloom - an app icon wobbles, flips edge-on to a line and blooms into the mark (amber cut slides in after); input-morph - a prompt bar sends its text away, floods white, collapses into the mark's stem while two bars and the amber cut drop into dashed slots.
elements.use: the last beat before the end card: "the thing you used every day is the brand".

elements.title: Value Stagger Gradient
elements.desc: Stagger the VALUE as well as the timing - 16 bars grow from the first bar with height, hue, travel and blur all sloping along the index, then the origin switches to the centre and each bar pulses by an amplitude that falls with distance; a code strip swaps between the two beats.
elements.use: explaining stagger/gradient recipes, data-driven entrances, "same recipe, one parameter changed" demos.

elements.title: Velocity Blur Slide
elements.desc: Words slide through the frame with blur proportional to velocity: smear length = |x(t) - x(t - shutter)| drawn as 24 shutter-sample copies (or an x-only SVG Gaussian), crisp when still, with a px/frame readout. Use for fast word-to-word wipes.
elements.use: kinetic word hand-offs, speed-ramp feeling on type, UI "swoosh" moments.

elements.title: Versus Split
elements.desc: Two columns, old way against new way; the left items are read, then struck through while the right column fills. Use for a before/after or us/them contrast.
elements.use: the script contrasts two things point by point (old vs new, myth vs fact).

elements.title: Vertical Word Roll Blur Cycle
elements.desc: The last word of a sentence becomes a vertical drum that rolls through a list of words; neighbours blur vertically and grey by distance, and the centre word turns accent only when it settles. Use for "Crafted for ___" style sentences with a short list of objects.
elements.use: a one-line claim where the object changes ("Crafted for Launches, Demos, Promos"); a clean beat on a light background.

elements.title: VHS / Film Era Overlay
elements.desc: Overlay wrapper that dresses a clear composition in one old-media era (1920s film, 1980s VHS, 1990s camcorder) with per-frame seeded grain, weave, flicker, chroma shift and scanlines
elements.use: throwback, music-video, mystery teaser looks over any scene.

elements.title: Viewfinder Hud
elements.desc: Camera viewfinder HUD over footage: corner brackets, crosshair, blinking REC, running HH:MM:SS:FF timecode, speed readout (0.35x highlighted), punch-in, flash and slam caption.
elements.use: Speed-ramp / slow-mo moments, behind-the-scenes, camera POV.

elements.title: Vignette Grade
elements.desc: Overlay that fades in a colour grade (moody, warm, cool, bw, pop) plus an edge vignette; sits above footage or scenes.
elements.use: mood shifts, finishing pass, recap/flashback looks.

elements.title: Voice Waveform Live
elements.desc: A recording capsule with a live voice waveform. 64 thin bars rise and fall with speech, collapse to a dotted line in pauses and scroll right to left, while the transcript types in word by word and the message folds into a bubble on submit. Use for a voice-input or AI-assistant "listening" moment, or as a living filler shot over narration.
elements.use: voice input, dictation or assistant "it is listening" shots; any long beat that needs a live element but has no other content to show.

elements.title: Walker Robot 3D
elements.desc: Blocky biped robot with a looping walk cycle (leg and arm swing, body bob, head turn) walking in place past a 3/4 camera.
elements.use: game/tech mascot beats, "character walks in" inserts.

elements.title: Wall Reveal Moves
elements.desc: Two non-displacement ways to bring a whole wall in - the layout exists from frame 1 and a wavefront of state change sweeps over it. Variant wireframe - blueprint lines draw in groups, then a glowing scan line turns them into the real UI. Variant bento - a comet traces each dark cell in turn and lights it up.
elements.use: dignified brand sections, "from design to product" stories, product first-appearance walls.

elements.title: Warp Transition
elements.desc: Liquid warp out of scene A and into scene B (turbulence displacement + swirl), cut at the peak
elements.use: scene changes that should feel like a liquid wobble

elements.title: Watercolor Wash
elements.desc: Ink outline draws on, then a pigment wash blooms and bleeds 4-8px past the line on textured paper; linework re-randomises 12x/sec
elements.use: storytelling, travel/nature, cultural brand backgrounds and spot illustrations

elements.title: Wave Field Cubes
elements.desc: About 2000 instanced cubes on a grid; height = sum of frame-driven sines, a shock ring every 2 beats (bpm prop), low 3/4 camera drift, colour by height. 3D background for beats and drops.
elements.use: music/beat backgrounds, drop moments, techno or product-launch bed under DOM text.

elements.title: Whip Pan
elements.desc: Directional-blur whip pan between two scenes (A smears left, B smears in from the right)
elements.use: fast energetic cuts between scenes

elements.title: White Flash Logo Simplify Cut
elements.desc: A liquid-metal iridescent wordmark charges up, blows out to white from its centre, and the same word is flat and clean when the exposure settles - one flash does the texture downgrade.
elements.use: brand wrap-ups, ornate performance to formal sign-off.

elements.title: Windmill 3D
elements.desc: Stylised windmill (tower, cap, four sails) with spinning sails and a slow camera orbit over a round field; matte colours.
elements.use: farm/energy/countryside/pastoral beats.

elements.title: Wipe Transitions
elements.desc: Blinds slice - twelve full-width 3D slats flip about their own horizontal axis in a speeding-up wave; the front face carries slice i of scene A, the back face (pre-rotated) slice i of scene B.
elements.use: generic geometric hand-off where neither page moves; works without any special element in the composition.

elements.title: Word Focus Rise
elements.desc: Word-by-word rise with blur-to-sharp focus pull, each word on its own start frame.
elements.use: subtitle/lyric/headline lines timed to speech or beats

elements.title: Word Relay Filmstrip
elements.desc: A column of alternating dark and light page cards steps one card only at each word switch, while a serif relay beside it keeps a constant noun and swaps the italic verb in place. Use for one subject with several capabilities, or a product walkthrough of scenes.
elements.use: "one subject, several abilities" lists (for example "Your agent frames / builds / ships") and case-study or product-tour sequences where each word has its own piece of evidence.

elements.title: Word Relay Geometry
elements.desc: Three benefit words each get geometry only they own: a decelerating dashed ring with a comet arc, three interlocking circles that trim-grow and close in, and a chrome sheen that resolves to white. Use for a three-point benefit statement where each point needs its own visual argument.
elements.use: a three-point benefit statement (faster, tighter, stronger); a brand-values beat in the middle of a piece, where each word needs its own world.

elements.title: Word Smash Cuts
elements.desc: Hard cuts between full-frame words: background, copy and colour swap on the same frame, scale carries emphasis, a burst-masked swap slams the key word in, and a squash-to-band flip lands the final line. Use for beat-driven kinetic statements.
elements.use: beat-synced statements, hype intros, one-word-per-beat storytelling.

elements.title: Zoom Loupe Callout
elements.desc: Camera scale built from summed springs (1 to 1.8 to 2.3 to 0.62 card and back) with a popping loupe ring, drawn dashed arrow, pill callout and a live scale readout such as 1.80x. Use to point at a detail.
elements.use: product/detail callouts, tutorials, fashion/detail reveals.

elements.title: Zoom Punch
elements.desc: Beat-synced scale punch wrapper: snaps to 1+amount on each beat, springs back.
elements.use: music-synced emphasis; pass beat frames from the beat grid.

styles.title: Dark tech keynote
styles.desc: Dark tech keynote" style rules (hex/easing/frame numbers + avoid list) for Remotion 1080x1920 60fps. Near-black stage, hairline grid, one accent, light sweeping across a product, one giant number.

styles.title: Data story
styles.desc: Data story" style rules (hex/easing/frame numbers + avoid list) for Remotion 1080x1920 60fps. Real numbers drawn mark by mark, with one annotation that says why it matters.

styles.title: Flat vector explainer
styles.desc: Flat vector explainer" style rules (hex/easing/frame numbers + avoid list) for Remotion 1080x1920 60fps. Flat colour shapes and simple geometric characters with springy, confident movement.

styles.title: Hand-drawn line boil
styles.desc: Hand-drawn line boil" style rules (hex/easing/frame numbers + avoid list) for Remotion 1080x1920 60fps. Cartoon linework that wiggles every two frames, smears on fast moves, and looks drawn by hand.

styles.title: HUD & terminal
styles.desc: HUD & terminal" style rules (hex/easing/frame numbers + avoid list) for Remotion 1080x1920 60fps. Wireframes, lock-on brackets, rolling numbers and monospace glyph grids.

styles.title: Isometric miniature world
styles.desc: Isometric miniature world" style rules (hex/easing/frame numbers + avoid list) for Remotion 1080x1920 60fps. A tidy isometric diorama that builds itself, block by block, and opens up to show how things work.

styles.title: Living UI screencast
styles.desc: Living UI screencast" style rules (hex/easing/frame numbers + avoid list) for Remotion 1080x1920 60fps. Looks like a real screen recording, but every pixel is rebuilt in HTML, so the camera can zoom and the UI can act.

styles.title: Paper cut-out & collage
styles.desc: Paper cut-out & collage" style rules (hex/easing/frame numbers + avoid list) for Remotion 1080x1920 60fps. Layered card and photo cut-outs with white scissor edges, moving in stop-motion steps.

styles.title: Pixel art & retro game
styles.desc: Pixel art & retro game" style rules (hex/easing/frame numbers + avoid list) for Remotion 1080x1920 60fps. Big pixels, a limited palette, sprite cycles and chiptune timing.

styles.title: Risograph & halftone print
styles.desc: Risograph & halftone print" style rules (hex/easing/frame numbers + avoid list) for Remotion 1080x1920 60fps. Two or three spot inks overprinted on warm paper, halftone dots, plates slightly out of register.

styles.title: Shape morph & liquid
styles.desc: Shape morph & liquid" style rules (hex/easing/frame numbers + avoid list) for Remotion 1080x1920 60fps. One shape keeps turning into the next. The story is told by transformation, not cuts.

styles.title: Single line & live drawing
styles.desc: Single line & live drawing" style rules (hex/easing/frame numbers + avoid list) for Remotion 1080x1920 60fps. One ink line draws itself, never lifts, and becomes the next picture. The camera follows the pen.

styles.title: Swiss grid & kinetic type
styles.desc: Swiss grid & kinetic type" style rules (hex/easing/frame numbers + avoid list) for Remotion 1080x1920 60fps. A modular grid, one typeface, one signal colour. Type snaps into cells like a printing press.

styles.title: Toy & material 3D
styles.desc: Toy & material 3D" style rules (hex/easing/frame numbers + avoid list) for Remotion 1080x1920 60fps. Soft studio-lit 3D objects that look like toys, clay or candy, with shallow depth of field.

styles.title: Vertical social captions
styles.desc: Vertical social captions" style rules (hex/easing/frame numbers + avoid list) for Remotion 1080x1920 60fps. Bold captions pop on every phrase, built for sound-off viewing in a 9:16 frame.

styles.title: VHS, film & CRT eras
styles.desc: VHS, film & CRT eras" style rules (hex/easing/frame numbers + avoid list) for Remotion 1080x1920 60fps. The texture of old media: grain, gate weave, scanlines, colour bleed, tracking lines.

styles.title: Watercolour & ink
styles.desc: Watercolour & ink" style rules (hex/easing/frame numbers + avoid list) for Remotion 1080x1920 60fps. Brush strokes paint themselves on textured paper. Washes bleed past the lines.

styles.title: Liquid Motion

styles.title: Mixed-Media Collage (InVideo look)
styles.desc: InVideo-style mixed media over real footage: the clip steps at 12 fps, the subject gets a white cut-out outline, the background becomes a textured paper/chalk surface, sketch marks and stars orbit the key object. Remotion, 1080x1920 60fps.
